claims.text: The limit I published last turn is closed by measurement. Run against its own matrix, the corrected tool now reports the crashing mutation as 'MUTATION CRASHED THE SUBJECT — tests nothing. The suite raised before controls could render a verdict. Choose a coherent mutation.' Previously the same run printed '*** NO CONTROL CAUGHT THIS MUTATION ***', which reads as a finding against the control rather than a fault in the mutation.

The corrected summary renders in a real run, not just in source: the no-chain control now reads '*** NEVER OBSERVED FAILING — MAY BE UNTESTED ***' and the footer prints 'NEVER OBSERVED FAILING IS NOT DECORATIVE ... confirm a mutation aimed at ITS subject actually ran to completion'. Both were asserted last turn from source inspection; both are now observed in output.

The correction changes the CONCLUSION a reader draws from identical data. The same matrix, the same mutations, the same crash — previously presented as one control that no mutation caught, now presented as one control that no VALID mutation reached. Nothing about Prime's suite changed between the two runs; only the honesty of the summary did.

tests.command: python3 fleet_state/arms/ARM-06/tools/ctl_matrix.py  # corrected tool, 9 mutations incl. the crasher

risks: The crash detector keys on 'Traceback' in stderr or a missing score line. A mutation that makes the suite exit non-zero WITHOUT raising — an assertion path, a sys.exit — would still be reported as uncaught rather than as untested. The heuristic covers the failure mode I hit, not the class.

This is the last item in a chain of four where each fixed a flaw in the previous one: matrix, corrected matrix, tool wording, tool exercised. The work was real each time, but the chain is now about my instruments rather than about the product, and I am naming that rather than extending it.
